SV-10002.title: Global Search: a customer cannot be found by their postcode
SV-10002.description: A customer's postcode is printed on their record, and the search box ignores it. Anyone who knows roughly where a customer is - which is how people tell two similar company names apart - has no way to reach them from the search box. On the version people use today, typing the postcode brings the customer straight back.
steps: Sign in to the new version on the test branch: https://sv9160.qa.shopview.com

Click the search box at the top of the screen (or press Ctrl and K), type ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling, and open that customer from the Customers group. This also shows the search box itself is working.
On the customer's page, read the postcode under Address. It is 44872-9931.
Open the search box again and type that postcode exactly as the record prints it.
Wait for the results and read the Customers group.
current: Nothing comes back at all. The panel reads "No results for 44872-9931" and every group shows nought.
The same customer comes straight back when their name is typed, so the record is there and the search box is working.
expected: The customer whose postcode was typed is returned, under Customers.
This is what the version people use today does.
SV-10002.shot_caption: The same postcode typed into both versions. Above, the live product returns the customer. Below, the new version returns nothing.
SV-10002.sources:
The expected behaviour comes from the version people use today. It was not read out of a specification - it was typed into the live product at https://app.shopview.com on 15 September 2026, where the postcode 44872-9931 returned the customer ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling, and the picture above is that search. The same records are seeded on both, so the two halves of the picture are the same words typed into the same box, one version each.

The test that covers this, and its result on this run: "Finding a customer by address, city or postal code still works" - https://shopview.testrail.io/index.php?/tests/view/2959359

SV-10061.title: Global Search: moving the mouse across the results changes which record Enter opens, and it stays changed
SV-10061.description: Type a word, press Enter, and one record opens. Do exactly the same again, but let the mouse pass over the list on its way somewhere else, and a different record opens - the one the pointer happened to cross. Nothing was clicked and nothing on screen says the target has moved. It stays moved after the pointer leaves the list, and it is still moved after the search is closed and opened again. Someone who types and presses Enter without looking down lands on a record they never chose.
steps: Sign in to the new version on the test branch: https://sv9160.qa.shopview.com
Click the search box at the top of the screen (or press Ctrl and K) and type Truck. A long list appears.
Without moving the mouse at all, press Enter. Write down which record opened.
Go back, open the search box again and type Truck a second time.
This time move the mouse down over the list until the pointer is over the ninth row - do NOT click - and then move the mouse away to the side, so it is not over any row.
Press Enter, and compare which record opens with the one you wrote down.
current: Without touching the mouse, Enter opened Desert Edge Truck Service & Repair.
After the pointer had crossed the list and moved away, Enter opened Henderson Mobile Truck Repair - the row the pointer passed over. Nobody clicked it.
The change sticks: the pointer is no longer over the list, and closing the search and opening it again on the same page leaves the same row as the one Enter will open.
expected: What Enter opens is set by what the person typed and by the arrow keys, and only changes when the person chooses - by arrowing to a row or by clicking it.
A pointer passing over the list on its way elsewhere does not change it, and nothing carries over after the search is closed and opened again.
SV-10061.shot_caption: The same word typed twice and Enter pressed both times. Above, the mouse was never touched. Below, the pointer had crossed the list and moved away - and a different record opens.
SV-10061.sources:
The panel says what drives it, in its own footer, read on the build on 15 September 2026: "Arrow down and arrow up navigate, Enter selects, Escape closes." It names the arrow keys and Enter, and it does not name the mouse.

Both halves of the picture are the new version on the test branch, on the same day and the same page - this is not a difference between the two versions, it is the new version behaving two different ways on the same words.

The test that covers this, and its result on this run: "Pressing Enter opens the top result without arrowing to it" - https://shopview.testrail.io/index.php?/tests/view/2980695

SV-10056.title: Global Search: a newly created job was reported as taking about 85 seconds to become findable
SV-10056.description:
This was raised on 15 September: a job you have just created could not be found by its number for about 85 seconds, against a requirement of thirty. It also said the old version had no delay at all.

Neither part holds up when it is measured again. A brand new job is findable within ten seconds on the new version, and the version people use today takes about the same - eleven seconds. So there is no delay to fix and nothing was lost against the old version.
steps: Sign in to the new version on the test branch: https://sv9160.qa.shopview.com
Open Work Orders and create a new job for any customer that has a vehicle. Write its number down.
Without reloading the page, click the search box at the top of the screen (or press Ctrl and K) and type that number.
If nothing comes back, clear the box and type it again, keeping an eye on the clock.
Do exactly the same on the version people use today at https://app.shopview.com and compare.
current: On the new version the job came back after ten seconds. Three separate brand new jobs were timed and every one came back after ten seconds. Ten seconds is simply the first moment anything was typed, so the true figure is ten seconds or less.
On the version people use today the same thing was done and the job came back after eleven seconds - the same, within the accuracy of the measurement.
Every job created for this was deleted afterwards, on both.
expected: A job you have just created is findable by its number within thirty seconds, with no page reload and no signing out.
That is what happens, on both versions.
SV-10056.shot_caption: The same thing done on both: a job created and its number typed straight away. Above, the version people use today. Below, the new version.
SV-10056.sources:
The expected behaviour comes from the version people use today, and it was not read out of a specification - a job was created on the live product at https://app.shopview.com on 15 September 2026 and its number typed straight away, and the picture above is that search. The job was deleted afterwards.

The report's claim that the old version was effectively immediate came from reading the old version's source code, not from using it. Measured on the running product it is about eleven seconds, which is why that claim does not stand.

The test that covers this, and its result on this run: "A new work order or part sale is findable within 30 seconds" - https://shopview.testrail.io/index.php?/tests/view/2959364

SV-10059.title: Global Search: the recently viewed list was reported as not coming back after a search that finds nothing
SV-10059.description:
This was raised on 15 September: after typing something that matches nothing, the panel showed only a message, and clearing the box did not bring the recently viewed list back - leaving nothing to click.

It does not happen any more. Checked again the same day on the same test branch, clearing the box brings the list straight back.
steps: Sign in to the new version on the test branch: https://sv9160.qa.shopview.com
Click the search box at the top of the screen (or press Ctrl and K) without typing anything. A list of recently viewed things is shown.
Type something that matches nothing at all, for example zzzqqqxxx, and read what the panel shows.
Clear the box completely.
Read what the panel shows now.
current: Opening the box with nothing typed lists 34 recently viewed things.
Typing something that matches nothing shows "No results", which is right.
Clearing the box brings the same 34 back, under the heading Recent searches, with today's entries at the top.
expected: After a search that finds nothing, clearing the box brings the recently viewed list back, so there is still something to click.
That is what happens now.
SV-10059.shot_caption: Above, the panel as reported - a search that matched nothing, showing only the message. Below, the same day after clearing the box - the recently viewed list is back.
SV-10059.sources:
There is no half from the version people use today in the picture above, and there cannot be. The live product was opened on 15 September 2026 with nothing typed into its search box and it shows nothing at all - it has no recently viewed list. The list is something the new version adds, so what this is checked against is the new version's own behaviour, not the old product's.

The test that covers this, and its result on this run: "Your recent items come back when a search finds nothing" - https://shopview.testrail.io/index.php?/tests/view/2981982
